Both the file and the tests use only the `.hom.app` form and apply the π-lemma by hand, never through simp. In Mathlib I read `cokernel.mapIso`, which is `@[simps]`, so `mapIso_hom` and `mapIso_inv` are simp lemmas. findings.problem: The file gives two simp rules that normalize the same component in different directions. `tensorNormalizedChainCokerNatIso_app` rewrites the `Iso.app` form `(iso).app (Arrow.mk f)` to `cokernel.mapIso …`. The `_hom_app` and `_inv_app` lemmas are also simp and have LHS `cokernel.π _ ≫ iso.hom.app (Arrow.mk f)`, in the `NatTrans.app` form. The ambient simp lemma `Iso.app_hom` turns `(iso.app X).hom` into `iso.hom.app X`. This competes with `_app`, because simp rewrites the inner `iso.app X` first. A goal written as `(iso.app (Arrow.mk f)).hom` therefore probably unfolds through `mapIso_hom` to `cokernel.map …`, and the π-lemmas then see no `iso.hom.app` and cannot fire. A goal written as `iso.hom.app (Arrow.mk f)`, which is the form every statement here and in the tests uses, keeps the `.hom.app` form and uses the π-lemmas. The same component can thus end in two different normal forms, `cokernel.map …` or `iso.hom.app …`, depending on how it was written. In addition, `_app` only gives a canonical form for `Iso.app`, while all downstream uses (including the test file) use `.hom.app`, so `_app` is unlikely to help them.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one canonical form. Keep the π-characterization lemmas as the simp interface for `.hom.app` and `.inv.app`, because they avoid unfolding `cokernel.map`. Then drop `@[simp]` from `tensorNormalizedChainCokerNatIso_app`, leaving it as an explicit `rw` lemma. Alternatively, keep it simp and add `tensorNormalizedChainCokerNatIso_hom_app'` and `_inv_app'` stating `iso.hom.app (Arrow.mk f) = (cokernel.mapIso … ).hom` and the inverse analogue, and drop `simp` from the π-lemmas. Whichever route is taken, state the orientation in the docstrings.
findings.benefit: Simp results no longer depend on whether a component was written as `(iso.app X).hom` or `iso.hom.app X`. Users get either a projection-based normal form (`cokernel.π ≫ …`) or an explicit `cokernel.map` form, not an unpredictable mix, and the lemmas stop competing.
